Teaching and feedback table variants use the Runner projections. Board facts are deterministic.

===== WORLD 19 · LESSON equilibrium_and_information · Equilibrium and information =====

TASK w19_1_teach [theory] Which claim does an equilibrium justify?
CAPTION: At equilibrium of a specified game, neither player can improve by changing strategy alone. A best response is a counter to a particular strategy. The Fundamental Theorem of Poker uses full information as a heads-up benchmark. Hidden cards limit which response you can choose.
TEACH: Which claim does an equilibrium justify? At equilibrium of a specified game, neither player can improve by changing strategy alone. A best response is a counter to a particular strategy. The Fundamental Theorem of Poker uses full information as a heads-up benchmark. Hidden cards limit which response you can choose.
Q: Which claim does an equilibrium justify?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] Against the equilibrium opponent, a unilateral change cannot improve expected payoff — Correct. Both strategies must belong to the same game and payoff model.
  - [wrong] The equilibrium maximizes profit against every actual opponent — Look again. A player who differs from the equilibrium can permit a more profitable targeted counter.
    BETTER ANSWER: Against the equilibrium opponent, a unilateral change cannot improve expected payoff
  - [wrong] Knowing the equilibrium reveals the opponent’s cards — Look again. A strategy predicts distributions and actions. Hole cards remain hidden.
    BETTER ANSWER: Against the equilibrium opponent, a unilateral change cannot improve expected payoff

TASK w19_1_read_information_value [drill] What action can that full-information benchmark separate?
CAPTION: In a heads-up exercise two possible river hands are K♣J♣ and 9♠9♦. BB uses the same river bet with either. You may compare one hidden-card policy with an oracle allowed to know which of the two is present.
Q: What action can that full-information benchmark separate?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: River | You Ah Qd | Board Qs 9c 6h 3d 2s | Pot 9.5 BB | To call 4 BB | Seat BTN | Active btn | Decision btn | Facts one pair, top pair
EFFECTIVE: BB 97.5
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ folded stack 100 BB | CO folded stack 100 BB | BTN dealer Ah Qd stack 97.5 BB | SB folded stack 99.5 BB | BB stack 93.5 BB bet 4 BB
TRAIL: preflop: SB posts 0.5 BB · preflop: BB posts 1 BB · preflop: UTG folds · preflop: HJ folds · preflop: CO folds · preflop: BTN raises to 2.5 BB · preflop: SB folds · preflop: BB calls 1.5 BB · flop: BB checks · flop: BTN checks · turn: BB checks · turn: BTN checks · river: BB bets 4 BB
  + [correct] Call against the miss and fold against the set — Correct. The oracle uses information unavailable in a real decision. The learner still needs weights and price.
  - [wrong] Call in both branches because the bet was the same — Look again. Identical actions do not make the two possible showdown outcomes alike.
    BETTER ANSWER: Call against the miss and fold against the set
  - [wrong] The oracle must also guess which card group is present — Look again. The premise grants full information to the benchmark.
    BETTER ANSWER: Call against the miss and fold against the set

TASK w19_1_day7_counter_changes_with_strategy [review] Which adjustment follows?
ENTRY: drill
CAPTION: Two otherwise comparable opponents use the same bet size. Their terminal betting ranges have identical value coverage. Player A adds enough misses that this bluff catcher clears the price. Player B adds no hands it beats.
Q: Which adjustment follows?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: River | You Ac Jd | Board Ah 7s 4c 2d 2h | Pot 10.5 BB | To call 5 BB | Seat BTN | Active btn | Decision btn | Facts two pair, paired board
EFFECTIVE: BB 97.5
SEATS: UTG folded stack 100 BB | HJ folded stack 100 BB | CO folded stack 100 BB | BTN dealer Ac Jd stack 97.5 BB | SB folded stack 99.5 BB | BB stack 92.5 BB bet 5 BB
TRAIL: preflop: SB posts 0.5 BB · preflop: BB posts 1 BB · preflop: UTG folds · preflop: HJ folds · preflop: CO folds · preflop: BTN raises to 2.5 BB · preflop: SB folds · preflop: BB calls 1.5 BB · flop: BB checks · flop: BTN checks · turn: BB checks · turn: BTN checks · river: BB bets 5 BB
  + [correct] Call A and fold B — Correct. The price stays fixed. Each opponent’s proportion of hands you beat changes the payoff.
  - [wrong] Call both because the price is identical — Look again. A shared price does not create shared equity.
    BETTER ANSWER: Call A and fold B
  - [wrong] Fold both because the same sizing hides the cards — Look again. Different modeled distributions still produce different estimates without revealing a hole card.
    BETTER ANSWER: Call A and fold B

===== WORLD 19 · LESSON population_response · Population response =====

TASK w19_2_teach [theory] Where should a pool tendency be applied first?
CAPTION: A pool read is an estimate for a specific game, stake, stack depth and line size. A population can overfold one node and underfold another.
TEACH: Where should a pool tendency be applied first? A pool read is an estimate for a specific game, stake, stack depth and line size. A population can overfold one node and underfold another.
Q: Where should a pool tendency be applied first?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] To the same line, size and pool that produced it — Correct. Segment the observations before transferring the policy.
  - [wrong] To every street for players on that site — Look again. A fold to a preflop raise does not imply a fold to a river overbet.
    BETTER ANSWER: To the same line, size and pool that produced it
  - [wrong] To every individual at that stake — Look again. An average does not erase variation across individuals.
    BETTER ANSWER: To the same line, size and pool that produced it

===== WORLD 19 · LESSON sample_and_segmentation · Sample and segmentation =====

TASK w19_3_teach [theory] Which sample best informs a 200 BB river spot against a regular?
CAPTION: Use stake, site, format, opponent type, depth and action history to filter a read. Small new samples should update a prior with uncertainty.

Q: Which sample best informs a 200 BB river spot against a regular?

TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] Comparable deep river spots from the same site and player type — Correct. Stack depth and player pool can change which hands reach the line and how they pay.
  - [wrong] A bigger list of 30 BB river spots from other sites — Look again. More mismatched observations still answer a different question.
    BETTER ANSWER: Comparable deep river spots from the same site and player type
  - [wrong] All preflop hands that the regular played — Look again. Most do not reach the relevant river decision.
    BETTER ANSWER: Comparable deep river spots from the same site and player type

===== WORLD 19 · LESSON opponent_adjusts · Opponent adjusts =====

TASK w19_4_teach [theory] What should make you retire an old exploit?
CAPTION: An exploit can lose its edge when the response changes. Mixed strategies can keep a line from identifying a single hand category.
TEACH: What should make you retire an old exploit? An exploit can lose its edge when the response changes. Mixed strategies can keep a line from identifying a single hand category.
Q: What should make you retire an old exploit?
HINT [hidden]: (none)
TABLE: Facts no applicable hand facts
  + [correct] Matched current observations that show the opponent defending more — Correct. A previous best response depends on a previous strategy. Re-estimate before repeating it.
  - [wrong] A single bluff lost at showdown — Look again. A positive-EV bluff still sometimes loses. The event is evidence, not a complete new distribution.
    BETTER ANSWER: Matched current observations that show the opponent defending more
  - [wrong] A winning showdown against their strongest hand — Look again. One result does not determine whether their fold or call frequency changed.
    BETTER ANSWER: Matched current observations that show the opponent defending more

  + [correct] The target calls with weaker hands and players behind usually release — Correct. You can often attain the desired heads-up position and keep a useful edge against the target.
  - [wrong] All players behind call every raise size — Look again. The raise may inflate a multiway pot and miss the isolation goal.
    BETTER ANSWER: The target calls with weaker hands and players behind usually release
  - [wrong] The target is the loudest person — Look again. Volume of speech does not describe the fold or call response.
    BETTER ANSWER: The target calls with weaker hands and players behind usually release

  - [wrong] Infer a single exact card combination — Look again. The model can remain a weighted range through the decision.
